source_text: A write-ahead log records every change to durable storage before the change is applied to the data files. After a crash the database replays the log from the last checkpoint to restore a consistent state. Checkpoints bound recovery time but cost extra disk writes.

source_text: The circuit breaker pattern wraps calls to a remote service and counts failures. When failures exceed a threshold the breaker opens and callers fail fast instead of waiting on timeouts. After a cool-down it lets a probe request through to test whether the dependency has recovered.

source_text: Consistent hashing maps both keys and nodes onto a ring. A key belongs to the first node clockwise from its position. Adding or removing a node only remaps the keys adjacent to it, rather than reshuffling the whole keyspace as modulo hashing would.

source_text: An LSM tree buffers writes in a memtable and flushes sorted runs to disk. Background compaction merges runs to bound read amplification. Writes are fast because they are sequential, but reads may need to consult several runs unless bloom filters rule them out.

source_text: TCP uses a sliding window to limit unacknowledged data in flight. The receiver advertises its window size, and the sender slows down when the window shrinks. Congestion control adds a second limit based on perceived network capacity.

source_text: Event sourcing stores state as an append-only sequence of events rather than overwriting rows. Current state is derived by folding the events, and snapshots avoid replaying the whole history. The cost is that schema changes to old events need careful versioning.
